items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: I got a scholarship to the Stan Kenton stage band camp at Indiana University, summer of ’63, and I got to study arranging with Herb Pomeroy.

ctx.x: Well to me, on my end, it sounds like your whole life has been like that. I’m sure that’s not quite true, but I’m going to go back to the Dallas recording things. When you were doing those things, bam-bam-bam one after the other, do you recall absorbing the idea of writing horn parts, listening — here’s my horn part, how does it fit with the person next to me and sort of storing that for later when you did it?

Oh absolutely. Well I started arranging when I was 13 so I understood the harmonies and stuff. I went to a small school, well a brief story of my life: My father was a US Navy pilot Pearl Harbor survivor. I was born in Honolulu in 1947 and I was a Navy brat until I was 11. And I had started playing violin when I was five so I played with the kiddy symphony in Honolulu, I played with the kiddy symphony in Garden Grove, Orange County, California, Pensacola Youth Symphony, blah-blah-blah.
